[RTIM.14.5] **Timeline replay.** The interpreter replays the `TestFact` timeline in
`(when_ns, source-order)` order ([LTSL.3.3]), advancing the mock clock across the
union of all input stamps, `TestCase.until_ns`, **scheduled reply deadlines** and
the **engine's deadlines** ([NLFC.2.5]) —
a delayed reply's deadline (`call_time + after_ns`, [RTIM.14.6]) is discovered
mid-run when the outbound call is issued, so the clock advances to it exactly as
to an input stamp. Before it moves the clock to any later instant, the interpreter
reads the engine's next deadline, and while that deadline is earlier than the
instant it moves the clock to the deadline and pumps there. At each instant the interpreter sets the clock, asserts, and
pumps to quiescence with the driving operations of [RTIM.5.1]; there is no
author-driven `pump` or `advance`. At a **shared instant**, input facts are applied **before** scheduled
replies, so the constructed input stream is well-defined: the interpreter builds
the asserted sequence, and [LDET.5] guarantees deterministic firing only given a
fixed stream, so this construction order is itself normative — a runtime that
delivered a co-timed reply before its input fact would diverge. An engine deadline
at the same instant as an input fact or a reply takes no step of its own: the
input facts and replies are applied first, and the one pump follows them.
